title: The lexical (pre-symlink) containment check in containedPath is unpinned and deletable with tests still green
detail: containedPath has two containment guards: a lexical check on the cleaned/abs path (lines 103-105) that fires before symlink resolution, and a real-path check after EvalSymlinks (lines 114-116). The symlink test TestCollectRejectsKnowledgeSymlinkOutsideRepo (knowledge_test.go:36) exercises only the SECOND guard: its escaping symlink is lexically inside root (`.beads/knowledge/external.jsonl`), so line 103's condition is false and its error return at 104-105 is never taken — the coverage profile shows 104.3,105.1 = 0 while the real-path error return 115.3,116.1 = 1 (covered). No test passes a path with `..`/traversal segments, so the lexical guard's rejection is enforced by nothing: lines 103-105 can be deleted and both tests still pass (the symlink case is caught by 114, the sorted-facts case never reaches the branch). The lexical check is the ONLY guard that returns the 'outside repository root' error for a non-existent traversal path (where EvalSymlinks at 110-113 would otherwise error first with a different message), yet that behavior is untested.
evidence: coverage profile: knowledge.go:104.3,105.1 = 0 (lexical error return uncovered) vs 115.3,116.1 = 1 (real-path error return covered by the symlink test).
suggested_fix: Add a test that reaches containedPath with a rel containing `..` (or otherwise lexically escaping root) and assert the 'outside repository root' error, pinning the lexical guard.
